title: kv-cache: improve memory management and eviction policies for fragmentation/paging/spillover
author: Ethan Park
description: Context: We observed increasing memory fragmentation and ineffective spillover behavior under mixed short/long-context workloads which led to elevated OOM/eviction churn and tail latency spikes. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes to KV cache memory management and eviction policies to reduce fragmentation, improve paging spillover heuristics, and make eviction decisions workload-aware. Motivation: Reduce per-request latency variance and lower token serving costs by keeping hot KV entries resident, compacting fragmented memory ranges proactively, and reducing unnecessary GPU-to-host spill/restore operations. Summary of changes: - Introduces a compacting allocator for KV segments that merges small free fragments when fragmentation crosses a threshold. The allocator can run incrementally on worker threads to avoid long pauses. - Adds an adaptive spillover policy that prefers paging large cold KV ranges to host memory and coalesces nearby cold entries to a single I/O unit to amortize spill cost. - Eviction scoring refactor: eviction score now combines recency, per-segment fragmentation score, entry size, and predicted reuse (based on simple LRU-decay + request-length histogram). - New background defragmentation task with backpressure rules tied to request load and GPU memory headroom to avoid interfering with latency SLOs. - Scheduler hooks so continuous-batching runtime can mark in-use KV ranges as protected during a batch window to prevent mid-batch evictions. - Observability/telemetry: added kv.cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv.cache.spill_ops_per_min, kv.cache.defrag_running, kv.cache.eviction_score_histogram, and tracing spans for spill/restore operations. - Tests: microbenchmarks for synthetic fragmentation patterns, end-to-end perf tests (mixed short/long chat workloads), and regression tests ensuring no increase in median latency under high load. Implementation notes: - The compacting allocator is implemented in runtime/kv_cache/allocator.cc and allocator.h with a best-fit coalescing pass that runs when a fragmentation_ratio > 0.25 or after N allocations (configurable). The compaction uses a work-stealing queue to allow multiple worker threads to compact disjoint ranges concurrently. - Spill coalescing groups adjacent cold pages within a 64KB window into a single spill file/chunk to reduce IOPS and GPU stalls. The coalescing window is dynamic: it expands when average spill latency is high and shrinks when restores dominate. - Eviction score uses a weighted sum: 0.5 * recency_score + 0.2 * size_penalty + 0.2 * fragmentation_penalty + 0.1 * reuse_prediction. We exposed weights as runtime-config flags to A/B during rollout. - Scheduling integration: continuous_batcher marks entries referenced during batch prep with a short-lived protection token; eviction ignores protected entries until token expiry. This reduced mid-batch tail latency spikes in tests. Backwards-compatibility and migration: - Default flags keep current behavior; new policies are gated behind runtime flags and an operator-visible rollout flag in /etc/redwood/kv_policy.conf for Dedicated/Private. We added migrations to zero-copy restore paths so older kernels can read coalesced spill files. Performance: - On internal mixed workload benchmark (50% short 16-token requests, 50% long 2048-token requests, 16-GPU node), merged changes reduce 95th token latency by 18%, eviction churn by 42%, and total GPU->host spill bytes by 36%. - Defragmentation cost measured as <2% additional CPU on the worst-case worker and was tuned to be idle during sustained 95th-percentile load. Rollout plan: - Start with Canary (1 cluster), enable adaptive spillover + eviction scoring weights A (safe defaults). - Monitor kv.cache.* metrics for 48h, then expand to 10% traffic with defrag disabled. - Enable full defrag and protection tokens at 50% after 72h of stable metrics, then full rollout. Notes for reviewers: - Focus review on allocator correctness (allocator.{cc,h}) and concurrency around compaction. I added a stress test that simulates concurrent allocation/free across 8 worker threads. - Verify spill file format change (runtime/kv_cache/spill_format.md) for compatibility notes. - CI: non-deterministic test in scheduler was flaky due to timing; I introduced a small scheduler tick jitter tolerance in tests. Related work: This builds on earlier spillover heuristics (see PRs: 170234, 176543, 179012) and replaces the previous reactive-only defrag with a prioritized incremental compaction approach.

review_comments: Ava Martinez: Left a few comments on allocator.cc around the fence ordering for compaction; please justify memory barriers.
Ethan Park: Thanks — added explicit atomic fences and updated comments to explain ordering. Added a stress test to reproduce and validate correctness.
Priya Gupta: Can you expose the fragmentation threshold as a runtime config and document safe defaults?
Ethan Park: Exposed fragmentation_threshold and compaction_idle_budget flags, documented in spill_format.md and rollout notes.
Liam O'Connor: Observability looks good. Suggest adding a span for coalesced_spill_group to make root-cause analysis easier.
Ethan Park: Added tracing span and wired it into spill_manager; updated dashboards to include group size histogram.
Ava Martinez: Approved pending one small comment fix on free-list duplication (fixed in last commit).
Priya Gupta: Approved after running canary locally and verifying metrics.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: incremental compaction to reduce fragmentation, adaptive spillover coalescing to lower I/O and restores, and workload-aware eviction scoring. Expected to reduce eviction churn and tail latency for mixed short/long workloads.
